subject: Clarify commit smoothing / packaging-conversion credits in Pricing Annex A
messages:
From: Emma Jenkins <procurement@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@acmehealth.com
Date: 2027-05-19 09:14:22 -0700
Subject: Clarify 'soft-minimum' language in Pricing Annex A

Ben —

Thanks for the Annex A draft. Our procurement team flagged the section titled 'soft-minimum protection' and asked for two clarifications before we can circulate internally:

1) Calculation example: the draft says Redwood will not pursue clawbacks for transient dips, but we need a worked example (90-day rolling, quarterly true-up) that shows how shortfalls are measured and when credits are applied versus when charges are invoiced.

2) Packaging conversion: our platform team will likely migrate % of SKUs mid-term during onboarding (bundle consolidation). Will the pricing conversion credit be applied pro rata from migration date, and how is the 'credit bank' funded and exhausted? We need the formula (net effective price delta or absolute price difference) so our finance can model impact.

I attached an annotated copy of your Annex with our inline questions (Acme_annotated_pricing.pdf). For transparency, legal wants the clause to protect customers undergoing a documented migration event (e.g., M&A or SKU consolidation) without creating a long-term escape hatch.

Can you put proposed redline language and an example calculation in your reply? If helpful loop in your legal.

—Emma
Emma Jenkins
Senior Procurement Manager, Acme Health
procurement@acmehealth.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jenkins <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-20 11:02:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify 'soft-minimum' language in Pricing Annex A

Emma — thanks for the annotated doc and clear asks. Attached is a first pass redline that attempts to balance Acme's migration concerns with Redwood's need to preserve commit economics (pricing_annex_redline_v1.docx). High level:

• Proposed renaming: replace 'soft-minimum protection' with 'commit smoothing window' to avoid implying permanence.

• Example calculation (illustrative): assume quarterly committed tokens = 10M. If actual tokens in rolling 90-day window fall to 9M (10% dip), we propose a smoothing credit equal to the shortfall * committed price * 50% (credit bank funded at 50% of the underage in the first true-up). Sustained underutilization (two consecutive quarters < 85% of commit) triggers a standard true-up invoice for the remaining shortfall.

• Packaging conversion credit: we propose a pro-rata credit from migration date using net effective price delta (old SKU effective unit price minus new SKU effective unit price) * quantity migrated * remaining days in committed period / total days in period. That way the credit reflects economic delta rather than gross list prices.

Questions for legal: is the 50% credit-bank cap reasonable or should we allow an indexed cap tied to the commit size? Also flagging levy of any clawback should be time-boxed (suggest 180 days from migration to claim).

Next steps: Lauren — can you review the attached legal framing and advise on wording that preserves our right to true-up while limiting clawbacks for documented migrations? Neha — FYI from quota/discount perspective. Emma — happy to hop on a quick 20-min call if you want to run the example live.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-22 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Clarify 'soft-minimum' language in Pricing Annex A

Ben/Emma — I reviewed Ben's suggested mechanics and pushed a legal-first redline (legal_redline_annexA.docx). Key changes I recommend:

1) Terminology and scope: define 'Commit Smoothing Window' as a rolling 90-day measurement period; explicitly exclude abuse (artificial batching or offloading traffic) and require written migration notice and basic migration evidence (migration plan + cutover date).

2) Credit mechanics: maintain Ben's pro-rata approach but replace the 50% shorthand with a formula: CreditIssued = Min( Max(ShortfallUnits * UnitPrice * 0.5, 0), ShortfallUnits * UnitPrice ). This caps credits at 100% of shortfall and floors at 0; it also leaves flexibility to negotiate the 0.5 multiplier per-deal.

3) Packaging conversion: require that conversion credits be calculated using 'Net Effective Price Delta' and require both parties to agree on the SKU mapping in writing within 30 days of migration. For mid-period migrations credits apply from the agreed migration date through the end of the current committed period, pro-rated by days.

4) True-up timing and discovery: Redwood may initiate a true-up no earlier than 180 days after the documented migration; discovery of continued underutilization beyond two consecutive smoothing windows allows Redwood to invoice the remaining shortfall with 30-day payment terms.

5) Audit and evidence: customer may present invoices/usage logs to substantiate migration; Redwood reserves a one-time audit right for credits > $50k.

These changes keep the smoothing protection genuine while protecting Redwood economics. If Acme wants a higher credit ratio for a short initial ramp (e.g., 75% credit bank for year 1) we can toggle the multiplier in the deal summary.

Ben — I left a few inline comments in the redline about 'materiality' and 'abuse' language; happy to reword for negotiation tone.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

Ben / Lauren — thanks, that addressed most of our concerns. A few final asks before we sign:

• Confirm the credit calculation uses net effective price delta (not gross list) — this is acceptable to our finance team.
• Add a short definitional table in the Annex that sets the 'migration date' and 'commit period' terms so there is no ambiguity about proration start/stop.
• Please add a single line that the credit bank is automatically exhausted before any cash refunds are issued (i.e., credits apply to future invoices first).

If you can incorporate those three edits into the next redline, we will route to Acme legal for a final review. We are aiming to finalize pricing terms and circulate for signatures next week. I also pasted our HubSpot deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-12345.
